samples.summary: `keepArchives` is a dead option whose doc comment names a caller this change removed
samples.evidence: `WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser(userId, { keepArchives })` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1135) and `eraseOfflineData(store, userId, { keepArchives })` (offline-erase.ts:30) both accept the flag, and the comment at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1166 says it is "for the one caller that did not ask for any of this: a session the server expired". A repo-wide grep for `keepArchives:` returns zero call sites — the expired-session path was instead rewired in `api/auth.ts` to pass `eraseLocalData: "none"`, which skips `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` altogether. The parameter is now unreachable and its comment documents a contract nothing exercises, so the archive-retention behaviour it describes is asserted by no test and reachable by no caller.

samples.summary: `OfflineRuntime` mounts for every signed-in session once the SDK pin is bumped, not only for users who opted in
samples.evidence: `const offlineInPlay = supportsClientKey() || getOfflinePersistenceEnabled(...)` is a disjunction, so the moment `@yorkie-js/react` goes past `MinClientKeyVersion` the left term is unconditionally true and `OfflineRuntime` mounts for every authenticated user. Its effect opens IndexedDB and issues its own unfiltered `GET /documents` (offline-runtime.tsx, `fetchDocuments()` in the reconcile block) on every session — hitting `packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:180`, whose query is `where: { workspaceId: { in: workspaceIds } }` across every workspace the user belongs to, unpaginated. The comment directly above (PrivateRoute.tsx:45-49) and the design promise it quotes — "a user who cannot even be offered the feature must not pay for it" / "declining the opt-in costs nothing" — describe a gate that only holds in the pre-bump direction. The out-of-diff sites that pay for it are every authenticated page load and that controller handler.

samples.summary: The documents/workspaces API modules now statically pull the whole offline IndexedDB stack into every consumer's module graph
samples.evidence: `api/documents.ts:6` adds `import { purgeOfflineDocuments } from "@/lib/offline-erase"`, and `offline-erase.ts` statically imports `./wafflebase-doc-store` (1,532 lines: IndexedDB schema, gzip via CompressionStream, eviction, archives), `./durable-session` and `./offline-persistence-preference`. `api/workspaces.ts:5` additionally adds a brand-new edge `workspaces -> documents`. Neither module previously depended on anything in `lib/` beyond types, and both are leaf API modules imported almost everywhere — e.g. `packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-list.tsx:116` (bulk delete), `components/app-sidebar.tsx` (fetchWorkspaces), and `packages/design-sandbox/scenes.config.json:96`, which renders `document-list.tsx` in sandbox scenes and therefore now loads the offline store too. Module-level evaluation is safe (no top-level `indexedDB`/`window` access outside a `typeof window` guard), so nothing crashes; the cost is that the per-chunk KB budget and every sandbox scene now carry code that only runs behind an opt-in nobody can enable yet.
searchedFor: read top-level statements of offline-erase.ts / durable-session.ts / offline-persistence-preference.ts

samples.summary: The headless unsaved-work probe was not revisited for the new `saved-locally` state, so the chunk-recovery reload now proceeds where it used to refuse
samples.evidence: `use-unsaved-work-probe.ts:24` still reads `const mayHaveUnsent = state === 'not-saved' || state === 'saving';`. A durable document with unsent edits now derives `'saved-locally'` instead of `'not-saved'` (sync-state.ts:85), so the probe never registers, `hasUnsavedWork()` (lib/unsaved-work.ts:38) answers `false`, and `lazy-with-retry.ts:158` and `:233` will take a recovery `window.location.reload()` that they previously refused. This is only safe under the assumption that a reload never detaches the document — the same diff extended the chip's *navigation* guard for `saved-locally` (`leavingLosesWork = mayHaveUnsent || savedLocally`) precisely because detach calls `removeFromStore` and deletes the durable entry. The probe is the sibling of that guard (its own docstring: "The `active` split matches the unload guard exactly") and is the only consumer that was left alone, so the assumption is now load-bearing and unasserted. Fix belongs here or in `lazy-with-retry.ts`, not in the new code.

samples.summary: `documentIdsIn`'s doc claims it lists folders, which `fetchDocuments()` does not return
samples.evidence: The new doc comment reads "The ids of every document this workspace holds, **folders included**", but the implementation is `fetchDocuments()` (api/documents.ts:35 -> `GET /documents`), which returns `Array<Document>`. Folders are a separate resource fetched by `fetchFolders(workspaceId)` in `packages/frontend/src/api/folders.ts:9`. Nothing breaks — folders hold no offline content — but the comment describes a contract the call does not have, and a future reader wiring folder cleanup would trust it.

samples.summary: Comment claims the runtime unmounts when navigating to Settings; Settings is inside `PrivateRoute`
samples.evidence: offline-runtime.tsx:230 says the component "unmounts whenever the authenticated shell does — navigating to a share link, to a public page, to Settings on a route tree of its own". `App.tsx:171` places `<Route path="/settings" element={<Settings />} />` inside `<Route element={<Layout />}>` inside `<Route element={<PrivateRoute />}>`, so the runtime — and with it `watchForOfflineDisable`, the only thing that performs the erase the Settings toggle promises — stays mounted on that route. The behaviour is correct; the comment describes routing that is not so, and it is the comment a reader would use to reason about whether the erase watcher is alive when the toggle is flipped.
